# Temple Scroll Column 39 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** 11QT (Cave 11), Col. 39 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**39:1** And you shall make a moat around the temple, outside the outer court, in order that they do not enter suddenly into My temple.

**39:2** And the moat shall be one hundred cubits wide and very deep.

**39:3** And between the moat and the outer court — a space of seven cubits; and they shall plant trees in it.

**39:4** And you shall make a parapet along the moat so that no one falls into it.

**39:5** And they shall not defile My temple by entering it suddenly in their uncleanness.

**39:6** And they shall sanctify My temple and fear My sanctuary, for I dwell among them.

**39:7** And you shall make latrines outside the temple city, to the northwest, at a distance from the city.

**39:8** And they shall go out to them — roofed places with pits within them — into which the filth shall descend.

**39:9** And they shall not be visible from the temple city at any distance.

**39:10** And no man shall go out to them on the Sabbath; the distance shall be three thousand cubits from the temple city.

**39:11** And you shall make three places to the east of the city, separated from one another, for the different types of uncleanness.

**39:12** And the places shall be for those who have skin diseases and for those who have discharges and for the men who have had an emission of seed.

**39:13** And they shall not enter the temple city until their purification is complete; and on the day of their purification they shall wash and be clean.

**39:14** And they shall bring their offerings as prescribed; and the priest shall pronounce them clean.

**39:15** And after that they may enter the temple city; and no unclean person shall be found in it.

**39:16** For it is the city of the temple; and I the LORD have hallowed it and set My name upon it; and it shall be holy forever.

---

*EMET notes: Column 39 describes the moat around the temple (vv. 1-5), latrines northwest of the city (vv. 7-10), and quarantine areas to the east (vv. 11-14). The Sabbath-distance rule for latrines (v. 10) parallels the Qumran War Scroll and Damascus Document. The 3,000-cubit distance reflects sectarian Sabbath-limit traditions.*
